- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); apply smoothing filter to dampen overshoots.
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above true outcome, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day from forecast to align with recent trend.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, assume momentum bias; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/– values), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
